h: Package slices defines various functions useful with slices of any type.

All.s: func slices.All[Slice ~[]E, E any](s Slice) iter.Seq2[int, E]
All.h: All returns an iterator over index-value pairs in the slice in the usual order.

AppendSeq.s: func slices.AppendSeq[Slice ~[]E, E any](s Slice, seq iter.Seq[E]) Slice
AppendSeq.h: AppendSeq appends the values from seq to the slice and returns the extended slice.

Backward.s: func slices.Backward[Slice ~[]E, E any](s Slice) iter.Seq2[int, E]
Backward.h: Backward returns an iterator over index-value pairs in the slice, traversing it backward with descending indices.

BinarySearch.s: func slices.BinarySearch[S ~[]E, E cmp.Ordered](x S, target E) (int, bool)
BinarySearch.h: BinarySearch searches for target in a sorted slice and returns the earliest position where target is found, or the position where target would appear in the sort order; it also returns a bool saying whether the target is really found in the slice. The slice must be sorted in increasing order.

BinarySearchFunc.s: func slices.BinarySearchFunc[S ~[]E, E, T any](x S, target T, cmp func(E, T) int) (int, bool)
BinarySearchFunc.h: BinarySearchFunc works like BinarySearch, but uses a custom comparison function. The slice must be sorted in increasing order, where "increasing" is defined by cmp. cmp should return 0 if the slice element matches the target, a negative number if the slice element precedes the target, or a positive number if the slice element follows the target. cmp must implement the same ordering as the slice, such that if cmp(a, t) < 0 and cmp(b, t) >= 0, then a must precede b in the slice.

Chunk.s: func slices.Chunk[Slice ~[]E, E any](s Slice, n int) iter.Seq[Slice]
Chunk.h: Chunk returns an iterator over consecutive sub-slices of up to n elements of s. All but the last sub-slice will have size n. All sub-slices are clipped to have no capacity beyond the length. If s is empty, the sequence is empty: there is no empty slice in the sequence. Chunk panics if n is less than 1.

Clip.s: func slices.Clip[S ~[]E, E any](s S) S
Clip.h: Clip removes unused capacity from the slice, returning s[:len(s):len(s)].

Clone.s: func slices.Clone[S ~[]E, E any](s S) S
Clone.h: Clone returns a copy of the slice. The elements are copied using assignment, so this is a shallow clone. The result may have additional unused capacity.

Collect.h: Collect collects values from seq into a new slice and returns it.

Compact.s: func slices.Compact[S ~[]E, E comparable](s S) S
Compact.h: Compact replaces consecutive runs of equal elements with a single copy. This is like the uniq command found on Unix. Compact modifies the contents of the slice s and returns the modified slice, which may have a smaller length. Compact zeroes the elements between the new length and the original length.

CompactFunc.s: func slices.CompactFunc[S ~[]E, E any](s S, eq func(E, E) bool) S
CompactFunc.h: CompactFunc is like Compact but uses an equality function to compare elements. For runs of elements that compare equal, CompactFunc keeps the first one. CompactFunc zeroes the elements between the new length and the original length.

Compare.s: func slices.Compare[S ~[]E, E cmp.Ordered](s1 S, s2 S) int
Compare.h: Compare compares the elements of s1 and s2, using cmp.Compare on each pair of elements. The elements are compared sequentially, starting at index 0, until one element is not equal to the other. The result of comparing the first non-matching elements is returned. If both slices are equal until one of them ends, the shorter slice is considered less than the longer one. The result is 0 if s1 == s2, -1 if s1 < s2, and +1 if s1 > s2.

CompareFunc.s: func slices.CompareFunc[S1 ~[]E1, S2 ~[]E2, E1, E2 any](s1 S1, s2 S2, cmp func(E1, E2) int) int
CompareFunc.h: CompareFunc is like Compare but uses a custom comparison function on each pair of elements. The result is the first non-zero result of cmp; if cmp always returns 0 the result is 0 if len(s1) == len(s2), -1 if len(s1) < len(s2), and +1 if len(s1) > len(s2).

Concat.h: Concat returns a new slice concatenating the passed in slices.

Contains.s: func slices.Contains[S ~[]E, E comparable](s S, v E) bool
Contains.h: Contains reports whether v is present in s.

ContainsFunc.s: func slices.ContainsFunc[S ~[]E, E any](s S, f func(E) bool) bool
ContainsFunc.h: ContainsFunc reports whether at least one element e of s satisfies f(e).

Delete.s: func slices.Delete[S ~[]E, E any](s S, i int, j int) S
Delete.h: Delete removes the elements s[i:j] from s, returning the modified slice. Delete panics if j > len(s) or s[i:j] is not a valid slice of s. Delete is O(len(s)-i), so if many items must be deleted, it is better to make a single call deleting them all together than to delete one at a time. Delete zeroes the elements s[len(s)-(j-i):len(s)].

DeleteFunc.s: func slices.DeleteFunc[S ~[]E, E any](s S, del func(E) bool) S
DeleteFunc.h: DeleteFunc removes any elements from s for which del returns true, returning the modified slice. DeleteFunc zeroes the elements between the new length and the original length.

Equal.s: func slices.Equal[S ~[]E, E comparable](s1 S, s2 S) bool
Equal.h: Equal reports whether two slices are equal: the same length and all elements equal. If the lengths are different, Equal returns false. Otherwise, the elements are compared in increasing index order, and the comparison stops at the first unequal pair. Empty and nil slices are considered equal. Floating point NaNs are not considered equal.

EqualFunc.s: func slices.EqualFunc[S1 ~[]E1, S2 ~[]E2, E1, E2 any](s1 S1, s2 S2, eq func(E1, E2) bool) bool
EqualFunc.h: EqualFunc reports whether two slices are equal using an equality function on each pair of elements. If the lengths are different, EqualFunc returns false. Otherwise, the elements are compared in increasing index order, and the comparison stops at the first index for which eq returns false.

Grow.s: func slices.Grow[S ~[]E, E any](s S, n int) S
Grow.h: Grow increases the slice's capacity, if necessary, to guarantee space for another n elements. After Grow(n), at least n elements can be appended to the slice without another allocation. If n is negative or too large to allocate the memory, Grow panics.

Index.s: func slices.Index[S ~[]E, E comparable](s S, v E) int
Index.h: Index returns the index of the first occurrence of v in s, or -1 if not present.

IndexFunc.s: func slices.IndexFunc[S ~[]E, E any](s S, f func(E) bool) int
IndexFunc.h: IndexFunc returns the first index i satisfying f(s[i]), or -1 if none do.

Insert.s: func slices.Insert[S ~[]E, E any](s S, i int, v ...E) S
Insert.h: Insert inserts the values v... into s at index i, returning the modified slice. The elements at s[i:] are shifted up to make room. In the returned slice r, r[i] == v[0], and, if i < len(s), r[i+len(v)] == value originally at r[i]. Insert panics if i > len(s). This function is O(len(s) + len(v)).

IsSorted.s: func slices.IsSorted[S ~[]E, E cmp.Ordered](x S) bool
IsSorted.h: IsSorted reports whether x is sorted in ascending order.

IsSortedFunc.s: func slices.IsSortedFunc[S ~[]E, E any](x S, cmp func(a, b E) int) bool
IsSortedFunc.h: IsSortedFunc reports whether x is sorted in ascending order, with cmp as the comparison function as defined by SortFunc.

Max.s: func slices.Max[S ~[]E, E cmp.Ordered](x S) E
Max.h: Max returns the maximal value in x. It panics if x is empty. For floating-point E, Max propagates NaNs (any NaN value in x forces the output to be NaN).

MaxFunc.s: func slices.MaxFunc[S ~[]E, E any](x S, cmp func(a, b E) int) E
MaxFunc.h: MaxFunc returns the maximal value in x, using cmp to compare elements. It panics if x is empty. If there is more than one maximal element according to the cmp function, MaxFunc returns the first one.

Min.s: func slices.Min[S ~[]E, E cmp.Ordered](x S) E
Min.h: Min returns the minimal value in x. It panics if x is empty. For floating-point numbers, Min propagates NaNs (any NaN value in x forces the output to be NaN).

MinFunc.s: func slices.MinFunc[S ~[]E, E any](x S, cmp func(a, b E) int) E
MinFunc.h: MinFunc returns the minimal value in x, using cmp to compare elements. It panics if x is empty. If there is more than one minimal element according to the cmp function, MinFunc returns the first one.

Repeat.s: func slices.Repeat[S ~[]E, E any](x S, count int) S
Repeat.h: Repeat returns a new slice that repeats the provided slice the given number of times. The result has length and capacity (len(x) * count). The result is never nil. Repeat panics if count is negative or if the result of (len(x) * count) overflows.

Replace.s: func slices.Replace[S ~[]E, E any](s S, i int, j int, v ...E) S
Replace.h: Replace replaces the elements s[i:j] by the given v, and returns the modified slice. Replace panics if j > len(s) or s[i:j] is not a valid slice of s. When len(v) < (j-i), Replace zeroes the elements between the new length and the original length.

Reverse.h: Reverse reverses the elements of the slice in place.

Sort.h: Sort sorts a slice of any ordered type in ascending order. When sorting floating-point numbers, NaNs are ordered before other values.

SortFunc.s: func slices.SortFunc[S ~[]E, E any](x S, cmp func(a, b E) int)
SortFunc.h:
SortFunc sorts the slice x in ascending order as determined by the cmp function. This sort is not guaranteed to be stable. cmp(a, b) should return a negative number when a < b, a positive number when a > b and zero when a == b or a and b are incomparable in the sense of a strict weak ordering.

SortFunc requires that cmp is a strict weak ordering. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weak_ordering#Strict_weak_orderings. The function should return 0 for incomparable items.

SortStableFunc.s: func slices.SortStableFunc[S ~[]E, E any](x S, cmp func(a, b E) int)
SortStableFunc.h: SortStableFunc sorts the slice x while keeping the original order of equal elements, using cmp to compare elements in the same way as SortFunc.

Sorted.h: Sorted collects values from seq into a new slice, sorts the slice, and returns it.

SortedFunc.s: func slices.SortedFunc[E any](seq iter.Seq[E], cmp func(E, E) int) []E
SortedFunc.h: SortedFunc collects values from seq into a new slice, sorts the slice using the comparison function, and returns it.

SortedStableFunc.s: func slices.SortedStableFunc[E any](seq iter.Seq[E], cmp func(E, E) int) []E
SortedStableFunc.h: SortedStableFunc collects values from seq into a new slice. It then sorts the slice while keeping the original order of equal elements, using the comparison function to compare elements. It returns the new slice.

Values.s: func slices.Values[Slice ~[]E, E any](s Slice) iter.Seq[E]
Values.h: Values returns an iterator that yields the slice elements in order.
